Main.sentence: Osama bin Mohammed bin Awad bin Laden [a] (10 March 1957 – 2 May 2011) was an Arab militant leader who was the founder and first general ___E:emir U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emir)___ of ___E:al-Qaeda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda)___ .

Ideologically a ___E:pan-Islamist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan-Islamism)___ , Bin Laden participated in the ___E:Afghan mujahideen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_mujahideen)___ during the ___E:Soviet–Afghan War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet%E2%80%93Afghan_War)___ of the 1980s, and supported the ___E:Bosnian mujahideen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnian_mujahideen)___ during the ___E:Bosnian War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnian_War)___ of the 1990s.

Opposed to ___E:American foreign policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_foreign_policy_in_the_Middle_East)___ in the ___E:Middle East U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_East)___ , Bin Laden ___E:declared war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_War_against_the_Americans_Occupying_the_Land_of_the_Two_Holy_Places)___ on the ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ in 1996 and advocated attacks targeting U.S. assets in various countries, and supervised the execution of the ___E:September 11 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ inside the U.S. in 2001.

Born in ___E:Riyadh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riyadh)___ to the aristocratic ___E:bin Laden family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bin_Laden_family)___ , he studied at Saudi and foreign universities until 1979, when he joined the mujahideen fighting against the Soviet invasion of ___E:Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan)___ .

In 1984, he co-founded ___E:Maktab al-Khidamat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maktab_al-Khidamat)___ , which recruited foreign mujahideen into the war. As the Soviet war in Afghanistan came to an end, Bin Laden founded al-Qaeda in 1988 to carry out worldwide jihad .

In the ___E:Gulf War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War)___ , Bin Laden's offer of support to Saudi Arabia against ___E:Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ba%27athist_Iraq)___ was rejected by the ___E:Saudi royal family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Saud)___ , which instead sought ___E:American aid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coalition_of_the_Gulf_War)___ .

___E:Bin Laden's views U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_views_of_Osama_bin_Laden)___ on pan-Islamism and ___E:anti-Americanism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Americanism)___ resulted in his expulsion from Saudi Arabia in 1991. He shifted his headquarters to ___E:Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_the_Sudan_(1985%E2%80%932019))___ until 1996, when he established a new base in Afghanistan, where he was supported by the ___E:Taliban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban)___ .

Bin Laden declared ___E:two U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fataw%C4%81_of_Osama_bin_Laden)___ fatāwā in August 1996 and February 1998, declaring ___E:holy war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_war)___ against the U.S.

After al-Qaeda's ___E:bombings of U.S. embassies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_United_States_embassy_bombings)___ in ___E:East Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa)___ , which killed hundreds of civilians, he was indicted by a U.S. district court and listed on the ___E:FBI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation)___ 's ___E:Most Wanted Terrorists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FBI_Most_Wanted_Terrorists)___ and ___E:Most Wanted Fugitives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FBI_Ten_Most_Wanted_Fugitives)___ lists.
In October 1999, the ___E:United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations)___ designated al-Qaeda as a terrorist organization.
Bin Laden organized the September 11 attacks, which ___E:killed nearly 3,000 people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casualties_of_the_September_11_attacks)___ , mostly civilians.

This resulted in the ___E:U.S. invading Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_invasion_of_Afghanistan)___ and launching the ___E:war on terror U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_terror)___ .
Bin Laden became the subject of a nearly decade-long ___E:international manhunt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhunt_for_Osama_bin_Laden)___ led by the U.S.
During this period, he hid in the mountains of Afghanistan and later escaped to neighboring ___E:Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan)___ .

On 2 May 2011, Bin Laden ___E:was killed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_of_Osama_bin_Laden)___ by U.S. special operations forces at ___E:his compound U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osama_bin_Laden%27s_compound_in_Abbottabad)___ in ___E:Abbottabad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbottabad)___ .

His corpse was buried in the ___E:Arabian Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Sea)___ and he was succeeded by his deputy ___E:Ayman al-Zawahiri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayman_al-Zawahiri)___ on 16 June 2011. During his lifetime, Bin Laden became a symbol of terrorism and was reviled in the United States and elsewhere as a mass murderer due to his orchestration of numerous attacks and bombings.
Bin Laden's name is most frequently rendered as "Osama bin Laden".

The ___E:Federal Bureau of Investigation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation)___ (FBI) and ___E:Central Intelligence Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency)___ (CIA), as well as other U.S. governmental agencies, have used either "Usama bin Laden" or the accepted transliteration "Usama bin Ladin".

Osama bin Laden's full name, Osama bin Mohammed bin Awad bin Laden, means "Osama, son of Mohammed, son of Awad, son of Laden".  "Mohammed" refers to Bin Laden's father Mohammed bin Laden; "Awad" refers to his grandfather, Awad bin Aboud bin Laden, a Kindite ___E:Hadhrami U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadhrami_people)___ tribesman.
Aboud's father was Ali, whose father was Omar. The family includes many individuals over a ___E:number of generations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bin_Laden_family#Family_tree)___ .

He was named Usama , meaning "lion", after ___E:Usama ibn Zayd U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usama_ibn_Zayd)___ , one of the ___E:companions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companions_of_the_Prophet)___ of ___E:Muhammad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad)___ .

Osama bin Laden had assumed the kunya (teknonym) Abū ʿAbdallāh , meaning "father of ___E:Abdallah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdallah_bin_Laden)___ " The Arabic ___E:linguistic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language)___ convention would be to refer to him as "Osama" or "Osama bin Laden", not "Bin Laden" alone, as "Bin Laden" is a patronymic, not a surname in the Western manner.

According to one of his sons ___E:Omar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omar_bin_Laden)___ , the family's hereditary surname is āl-Qaḥṭānī , but Bin Laden's father, ___E:Muhammad bin Ladin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_bin_Ladin)___ , never officially registered the name.
Osama bin Laden was born on 10 March 1957 in ___E:Riyadh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riyadh)___ , Saudi Arabia.

His father was ___E:Muhammad bin Ladin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_bin_Ladin)___ ,   a ___E:Yemeni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemenis)___ -born billionaire construction magnate with close ties to the ___E:Saudi royal family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Saud)___ ,  and his mother was Mohammed bin Laden's tenth wife, ___E:Syrian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian)___ ___E:Hamida al-Attas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamida_al-Attas)___ (then called Alia Ghanem).

Despite it being generally accepted that Bin Laden was born in Riyadh, his birthplace was listed as ___E:Jeddah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeddah)___ in the initial FBI and ___E:Interpol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpol)___ documents.
Mohammed bin Laden divorced Hamida soon after Osama bin Laden was born. Mohammed recommended Hamida to Mohammed al-Attas, an associate.
Al-Attas married Hamida in the late 1950s or early 1960s.
The couple had four children, and Bin Laden lived in the new household with three half-brothers and one half-sister.
The Bin Laden family made $5 billion in the construction industry, of which Osama later inherited around $25–30 million.
Bin Laden was raised as a devout ___E:Sunni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunni)___ Muslim.
From 1968 to 1976, he attended the elite ___E:Al-Thager Model School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Thager_Model_School)___ .

Bin Laden attended an English-language course in ___E:Oxford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford)___ , England, during 1971.  He studied ___E:economics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics)___ and ___E:business administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_administration)___  at ___E:King Abdulaziz University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Abdulaziz_University)___ .

Some reports suggest he earned a degree in ___E:civil engineering U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_engineering)___ in 1979,  or a degree in ___E:public administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_administration)___ in 1981.  One source described him as "hard working";  another said he left university during his third year without completing a college degree.

At university, Bin Laden's main interest was religion, where he was involved in both "interpreting the ___E:Quran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quran)___ and jihad " and charitable work.  Other interests included writing poetry; reading, with the works of Field Marshal ___E:Bernard Montgomery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Montgomery)___ and ___E:Charles de Gaulle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_de_Gaulle)___ said to be among his favorites; black ___E:stallions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stallion)___ ; and ___E:association football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football)___ , in which he enjoyed playing at ___E:centre forward U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre-forward)___ and followed the English club ___E:Arsenal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C.)___ .

During his studies in Jeddah, Bin Laden became a pupil of the influential Islamist scholar ___E:Abdullah Yusuf Azzam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdullah_Yusuf_Azzam)___ and avidly read his treatises.

He also read the writings of several ___E:Muslim Brotherhood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_Brotherhood)___ leaders and was highly influenced by the Islamic revolutionary ideas advocated by ___E:Sayyid Qutb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sayyid_Qutb)___ .

At age 17 in 1974, Bin Laden married ___E:Najwa Ghanem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Najwa_Ghanem)___ at ___E:Latakia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latakia)___ , Syria;  however, they were later separated and she left Afghanistan on 9 September 2001, two days before the 9/11 attacks.
His other known wives were Khadijah Sharif (married 1983, divorced 1993); Khairiah Sabir (married 1985); Siham Sabir (married 1987); and Amal al-Sadah (married 2000).
Some sources also list a sixth wife, name unknown, whose marriage to Bin Laden was annulled soon after the ceremony.
Bin Laden fathered 24 children with his wives.
Many of Bin Laden's children fled to Iran following the September 11 attacks, and as of 2010 [update] Iranian authorities closely controlled them there.
___E:Nasser al-Bahri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasser_al-Bahri)___ , who was Bin Laden's personal bodyguard from 1997 to 2001, details Bin Laden's personal life in his memoir.
He describes him as a frugal man and strict father, who enjoyed taking his large family on shooting trips and picnics in the desert.
Bin Laden's father Mohammed died in 1967 in an airplane crash in Saudi Arabia when his American pilot Jim Harrington  misjudged a landing.

Bin Laden's eldest half-brother, ___E:Salem bin Laden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salem_bin_Laden)___ , the subsequent head of the Bin Laden family, was killed in 1988 near ___E:San Antonio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio)___ , Texas, in the U.S., when he accidentally flew a plane into power lines.

The FBI described Bin Laden as an adult as tall and thin, between 1.93 m (6 ft 4 in) and 1.98 m (6 ft 6 in) in height and weighing about 73 kilograms (160 lb),  although author ___E:Lawrence Wright U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Wright)___ , in his book on ___E:al-Qaeda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda)___ , The Looming Tower , writes that a number of Bin Laden's close friends confirmed that reports of his height were greatly exaggerated, and that he was actually "just over 6 feet (1.8 m) tall".
After his death, he was measured to be roughly 1.93 m (6 ft 4 in).

Bin Laden had an ___E:olive complexion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olive_skin)___ and was left-handed, usually walking with a cane. He wore a plain white ___E:keffiyeh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keffiyeh)___ .
At one point, he stopped wearing the traditional Saudi male keffiyeh and instead wore the traditional Yemeni male keffiyeh.
He was described as soft-spoken and mild-mannered in demeanor.

According to former CIA analyst ___E:Michael Scheuer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Scheuer)___ , who led the CIA's hunt for Bin Laden, Bin Laden was motivated by a belief that ___E:U.S. foreign policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_foreign_policy)___ has oppressed, killed, or otherwise harmed Muslims in the Middle East.  As such, the threat to U.S. national security arises not from al-Qaeda being offended by what the U.S. is but rather by what the U.S. does, or in the words of Scheuer, "They (al-Qaeda) hate us (Americans) for what we do, not who we are."  Nonetheless, Bin Laden criticized the U.S. for its ___E:secular U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secular)___ form of governance, calling upon Americans to convert to Islam and reject the immoral acts of ___E:fornication U:(https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/fornication)___ , ___E:homosexuality U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuality)___ , ___E:intoxicants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychoactive_drug)___ , ___E:gambling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gambling)___ , and ___E:usury U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usury)___ , in a letter published in late 2002.

Bin Laden believed that the Islamic world was in crisis and that the complete restoration of ___E:Sharia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharia)___ law would be the only way to set things right in the Muslim world.

He opposed such alternatives as secular government,  as well as ___E:pan-Arabism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan-Arabism)___ , ___E:socialism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialism)___ , ___E:communism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communism)___ , and ___E:democracy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democracy)___ .
He subscribed to the ___E:Athari U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athari)___ (literalist) school of ___E:Islamic theology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schools_of_Islamic_theology)___ .

These beliefs, in conjunction with violent jihad , have sometimes been called ___E:Qutbism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qutbism)___ after being promoted by ___E:Sayyid Qutb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sayyid_Qutb)___ .

Bin Laden believed that Afghanistan, under the rule of ___E:Mullah Omar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mullah_Omar)___ 's ___E:Taliban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban)___ , was "the only Islamic country" in the Muslim world.
Bin Laden consistently dwelt on the need for violent jihad to right what he believed were injustices against Muslims perpetrated by the U.S. and sometimes by other non-Muslim states.

In his Letter to the American People published in 2002, Bin Laden described the formation of the ___E:Israeli state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_state)___ as "a crime which must be erased" and demanded that the United States withdraw all of its civilians and military personnel from the ___E:Arabian Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Peninsula)___ , as well as from all ___E:Muslim lands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar_al-islam)___ .

His viewpoints and methods of achieving them had led to him being designated as a terrorist by scholars;   journalists from The New York Times ,   the ___E:BBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC)___ ,  and Qatari news station ___E:Al Jazeera U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Jazeera_Media_Network)___ ;  and analysts such as ___E:Peter Bergen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Bergen)___ ,  Michael Scheuer,  ___E:Marc Sageman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Sageman)___ ,  and ___E:Bruce Hoffman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Hoffman)___ .

He was indicted on terrorism charges by law enforcement agencies in ___E:Madrid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid)___ , New York City, and ___E:Tripoli U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tripoli,_Libya)___ .
Bin Laden supported the targeting of American civilians, in retaliation against U.S. troops indiscriminately attacking Muslims.
He asserted that this policy could deter U.S. troops from targeting Muslim women and children.
Furthermore, he argued that all Americans were complicit in the crimes of their government due to majority of them electing it to power and paying taxes that fund the U.S. military.

According to ___E:Noah Feldman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_Feldman)___ , Bin Laden's assertion was that "since the United States is a democracy, all citizens bear responsibility for its government's actions, and civilians are therefore fair targets."

Two months after the ___E:September 11, 2001 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ , Bin Laden stated during an interview with Pakistani journalist ___E:Hamid Mir U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamid_Mir)___ :

"According to my information, if the enemy occupies an Islamic land and uses its people as ___E:human shields U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_shields)___ , a person has the right to attack the enemy. ...
The targets of September 11 were not women and children.
The main targets were the symbol of the United States: their economic and military power.
Our ___E:Prophet Muhammad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prophet_Muhammad)___ was against the killing of women and children.
When he saw the body of a non-Muslim woman during a war, he asked what the reason for killing her was. If a child is older than thirteen and bears arms against Muslims, killing him is permissible."

Bin Laden's overall strategy for achieving his goals against much larger enemies such as the ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union)___ and U.S. was to lure them into a long ___E:war of attrition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attrition_warfare)___ in Muslim countries, attracting large numbers of jihadists who would never surrender.
He believed this would lead to ___E:economic collapse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_collapse)___ of the enemy countries, by "bleeding" them dry.  Al-Qaeda manuals express this strategy.
In a ___E:2004 tape U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Osama_bin_Laden_video)___ broadcast by Al Jazeera, Bin Laden spoke of "bleeding America to the point of bankruptcy".

A number of errors and inconsistencies in Bin Laden's arguments have been alleged by authors such as ___E:Max Rodenbeck U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Rodenbeck)___ and ___E:Noah Feldman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_Feldman)___ .

He invoked democracy both as an example of the deceit and fraudulence of ___E:Western political system U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_world#Modern_political)___ —American law being "the law of the rich and wealthy"  —and as the reason civilians are responsible for their government's actions and so can be lawfully punished by death.

He denounced democracy as a "religion of ignorance" that violates Islam by issuing man-made laws, but in a later statement compares the Western democracy of Spain favorably to the Muslim world in which the ruler is accountable.

Rodenbeck states, "Evidently, [Bin Laden] has never heard theological justifications for democracy, based on the notion that the will of the people must necessarily reflect the will of an all-knowing God."

Bin Laden was heavily ___E:anti-Semitic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitism)___ , stating that most of the negative events that occurred in the world were the direct result of Jewish actions.

In a December 1998 interview with Pakistani journalist ___E:Rahimullah Yusufzai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahimullah_Yusufzai)___ , Bin Laden stated that ___E:Operation Desert Fox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Desert_Fox)___ was proof that ___E:Israeli Jews U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Jews)___ controlled the governments of the U.S. and the United Kingdom, directing them to kill as many Muslims as they could.
In a letter released in late 2002, he stated that Jews controlled the civilian media outlets, politics, and economic institutions of the United States.

In a May 1998 interview with ___E:ABC News U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(United_States))___ , Bin Laden claimed that the Israeli state's ultimate goal was to annex the Arabian Peninsula and the Middle East into its territory and enslave its peoples, as part of what he called a " ___E:Greater Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Israel)___ ".

He stated that Jews and Muslims could never get along, that war was "inevitable" between them, and accusing the U.S. of stirring up ___E:anti-Islamic sentiment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criticism_of_Islam)___ .

He claimed that the ___E:U.S. State Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_State_Department)___ and ___E:U.S. Department of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Department_of_Defense)___ were controlled by Jews, for the sole purpose of serving the Israeli state's goals.
He often delivered warnings against alleged Jewish conspiracies: "These Jews are masters of usury and leaders in treachery.

They will leave you nothing, either in this world or the next."  ___E:Shia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia)___ Muslims have been listed along with ___E:heretics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heretics)___ , the United States, and Israel as the four principal enemies of Islam at ideology classes of Bin Laden's al-Qaeda organization.
Bin Laden was opposed to music on religious grounds,  and his attitude towards technology was mixed.

He was interested in earth-moving machinery and ___E:genetic engineering U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_engineering)___ of plants, while rejecting the use of ___E:chilled water U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilled_water)___ .

He also believed ___E:climate change U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change)___ to be a serious threat and penned a letter urging Americans to work with U.S. president ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ to make a rational decision to "save humanity from the harmful gases that threaten its destiny".

After leaving college in 1979, Bin Laden went to Pakistan, joined Abdullah Yusuf Azzam and used money and machinery from his own construction company to help the mujahideen resistance in the ___E:Soviet–Afghan War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet%E2%80%93Afghan_War)___ .

He later told a journalist: "I felt outraged that an injustice had been committed against the people of Afghanistan."  From 1979 to 1992, the U.S. (as part of ___E:CIA activities in Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIA_activities_in_Afghanistan)___ , specifically ___E:Operation Cyclone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Cyclone)___ ), Saudi Arabia, and ___E:China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China)___ provided between $6–12 billion worth of financial aid and weapons to tens of thousands of mujahideen through Pakistan's ___E:Inter-Services Intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter-Services_Intelligence)___ (ISI).
British journalist ___E:Jason Burke U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Burke)___ wrote: "[Bin Laden] did not receive any direct funding or training from the U.S. during the 1980s.
Nor did his followers.

The Afghan mujahideen , via Pakistan's ISI intelligence agency, received large amounts of both. Some bled to the Arabs fighting the Soviets but nothing significant."  Bin Laden met and built relations with ___E:Hamid Gul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamid_Gul)___ , who was a ___E:three-star U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-star_rank)___ ___E:general U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_General_(Pakistan))___ in the ___E:Pakistani Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Army)___ and head of the ISI agency.

Although the United States provided the money and weapons, the training of militant groups was entirely done by the ___E:Pakistan Armed Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Armed_Forces)___ and the ISI.
